title: Our Home
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 2 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child tells personal items from common items at home, says personal items are not shared, and names cleaning materials for each.

floor.prerequisite: Knows materials for cleaning the body.
floor.question: What do we use to clean our teeth?
floor.answer: A toothbrush and toothpaste (or a chewing stick)

representations: real items: toothbrush, comb, plate, cup, broom
soap, ash, a brush and a cloth
steps: Sort them into personal and common.
Say which must not be shared.
Match each to a cleaning material.
contexts: a family of six sharing a house

board.do: Draw a toothbrush, a comb, a table and a broom.
Wait for the child to say personal and why.
Write P or C under each.

misconceptions.ask: Can you share your toothbrush with your sister?
misconceptions.repair: Sort items into "mine only" and "for everyone". Say: some things carry germs from one mouth to another.

misconceptions.ask: Is the sofa at home a personal item or a common item?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: who else uses it? If many people use it, it is common.

misconceptions.ask: What do you need to clean an oily plate?
misconceptions.repair: Wash one oily plate with water only and one with soap. Feel both.

listen_for: Common, it hangs where everyone bathes
misconceptions.ask: Is your bathing towel a personal or common item?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what the towel touches: your body. Items that touch the body are personal.

checks.question: Is a comb personal or common?
What do we use to clean a dirty pot?
